requirement: Whenever the air vehicle operates within its assigned operational radius of approximately 1 km from the ground control station, command and telemetry link availability shall be maintained at an acceptable level, with uplink and downlink availability each expressed as at least 95 across the mission profile.

instances.explanation: 'acceptable' judges link availability by subjective operator satisfaction rather than a defined figure, so what counts as an acceptable level is reader-dependent.
the value 95 is given with no unit of measure — percent availability, dB margin, or something else — so the actual availability figure cannot be verified.
the passive 'shall be maintained' does not name which actor — the datalink subsystem, the C2 radio transceiver, or ground crew — is responsible for sustaining link availability.

requirement: When the flight control system initiates the command-and-control interface to the ground control station, the datalink subsystem shall not release telemetry data to the controller without confirmation that the encrypted session handshake has completed.

instances.explanation: 'the controller' is a bare common noun without which-one binding — it could be the onboard flight control system's autopilot function or a separate ground-side control console — so who receives the telemetry release is unclear.

instances.trigger: shall not release telemetry data to the controller without confirmation
instances.explanation: the negation's scope is unclear: it may mean release is merely deferred until confirmation arrives, or that release is categorically forbidden except in the narrow case where confirmation is already present, changing what is permitted before the handshake completes.

requirement: While operating beyond visual line of sight, the datalink subsystem shall encrypt the command-and-control channel to the same standard as the telemetry downlink, and it shall authenticate the ground control station before accepting any command traffic.

instances.explanation: the elided comparison is recoverable two ways — encrypted to whatever standard the telemetry downlink itself happens to use, or encrypted to a separately specified standard that merely matches the telemetry downlink's rigor — so the required cipher strength is unclear.
'it' has more than one candidate antecedent in the preceding clause — the datalink subsystem or the command-and-control channel — so which entity must perform the authentication is unclear.

requirement: If the command-and-control link is lost for longer than 3 seconds, the flight control system shall command the air vehicle to enter return-to-launch, the receiver shall continue attempting to reacquire the link at fixed intervals, and the flight control system shall report link-loss status to the operator once contact is restored.

instances.explanation: 'the receiver' is a bare common noun with no which-one binding — it could denote the airborne C2 radio transceiver's receive path or the ground control station's receiver — so which hardware is responsible for reacquisition attempts is unclear.

requirement: The datalink subsystem shall establish the command-and-control uplink between the ground control station and the C2 radio transceiver, and it shall relay telemetry from the flight control system to the ground control station over the telemetry modem. Upon completing link establishment, the datalink subsystem shall report its current link mode to the operator promptly. The C2 uplink shall re-acquire lock faster than the telemetry downlink whenever a momentary dropout occurs. Following the vertical-takeoff phase, the datalink subsystem shall reduce command uplink signal margin monitoring shortly after transition to cruise link mode.

instances.explanation: 'mode' is polysemous — it can mean the datalink's frequency/channel mode or the operational link state such as acquisition, tracking, or lost-lock — so which kind of mode must be reported is unclear.

the elided comparison is recoverable two ways — the C2 uplink re-acquires lock faster than the telemetry downlink re-acquires its own lock, or faster than the telemetry downlink's specified reacquisition baseline — so what exactly is being compared is unclear.
'promptly' states no numeric bound on how quickly the link mode must be reported after establishment.

the noun stack 'command uplink signal margin' can parse as (command-uplink)(signal-margin), the signal margin of the command uplink, or as (command)(uplink-signal-margin), a general uplink-signal-margin parameter as it pertains to commands, leaving the intended quantity structurally ambiguous.
'shortly' states no numeric bound on how soon after the cruise transition monitoring is reduced.

requirement: While operating within its designated frequency band, the datalink subsystem shall sustain a telemetry downlink throughput of at least 50, and it shall keep command-channel latency low enough for real-time control.

requirement: Building on the throughput and latency bounds established above, the datalink subsystem shall interface with the flight control system with a deterministic message queue for command injection. The datalink subsystem may buffer telemetry frames if needed before handoff to the C2 radio transceiver. The datalink subsystem shall support the flight control system's health-telemetry stream at the rate defined for that bound, and the datalink subsystem shall expose a waypoint update channel accepting a waypoint from the ground control station.

'may ... if needed' leaves the buffering obligation optional and does not state the criterion that makes buffering necessary, so it is unverifiable.
'a waypoint' can be read as a specific waypoint token being sent in the moment, or as the general type/class of waypoint messages the channel accepts, so what the channel must accommodate is unclear.

requirement: When the C2 radio transceiver regains signal after a dropout, the datalink subsystem shall resume telemetry streaming to the ground control station, it shall re-synchronize its command sequence numbering with the flight control system, and it shall notify the operator shortly after resynchronization completes.

instances.explanation: 'resume' presupposes a specific prior streaming state to return to, but it is unclear whether streaming resumes from the last packet sent before the dropout or restarts as a fresh stream from the current telemetry state.

requirement: The datalink subsystem shall monitor link quality with the signal-strength indicator at a reporting threshold specified elsewhere, without suppressing a degraded-link report absent operator acknowledgment. The datalink subsystem may hand over reporting duty to the ground control station's own signal meter as required.

'hand over' can be read literally, as physically transferring equipment, or figuratively, as delegating reporting responsibility, leaving the intended action unclear.
the actual reporting threshold value is deferred to an unnamed external document rather than stated here, leaving the trigger condition unquantified.

the scope of 'without suppressing' is unclear: it may forbid suppressing a report only until acknowledgment arrives, or forbid suppression outright except in the narrow case where acknowledgment already exists, changing what is permitted before acknowledgment.
'as required' does not state who determines when handing over reporting duty is required, making the obligation's trigger unverifiable.

requirement: Prior to vertical takeoff, the datalink subsystem shall calibrate the C2 radio transceiver and the telemetry modem or the backup receiver, verifying link margin with the ground station before releasing the aircraft for flight. instances.explanation: 'the operator' can be read generically, as any qualified operator role, or non-generically, as the one specific individual assigned to this mission, leaving unclear whose retained control is being guaranteed.

requirement: While interfacing with the datalink subsystem, the command uplink buffer shall retain both queued commands and pending acknowledgments or discard the oldest entry when capacity is reached. requirement: While operating in degraded link mode, the datalink power amplifier shall reduce transmit output to 2 W and hold that level until the C2 radio transceiver confirms nominal signal-to-noise ratio. Once nominal mode resumes, the datalink power amplifier shall restore full transmit output within 2 seconds.
